title: A finite-length module has a filtration with simple quotients
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module of finite length, i.e. $\mathrm{length}_R(M)<\infty$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Then there are an integer $r\ge0$ and $R$-submodules $0=M_0\subsetneq M_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq M_r=M$ such that each quotient $M_i/M_{i-1}$ ($1\le i\le r$) is simple [def-weil-pbc-simple-module]: it is nonzero and has no $R$-submodule other than $0$ and itself.

source.place: Algebra, Definition Tag 02LY (definition-length, line 12350), Definition Tag 00J1 (definition-simple-module, line 12508) and Lemma Tag 00J3 (lemma-simple-pieces, line 12546, part (2) and the first sentence of its proof): a maximal chain in a finite-length module has simple successive quotients

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Module.length_ne_top_iff to the inequality length_R(M) < infinity [def-weil-pbc-module-length], obtaining IsFiniteLength R M. Apply isFiniteLength_iff_exists_compositionSeries to obtain a composition series s of Submodule R M with head zero and last M. Set r = s.length and F = s.toFun; RelSeries.head and RelSeries.last give the required endpoints.

For each i in Fin r, s.step i states that F(i.castSucc) is covered by F(i.succ); its lt field gives the required strict inequality. Apply Mathlib covBy_iff_quot_is_simple to the le field and the same covering relation. This gives IsSimpleModule R (F(i.succ) / comap (F(i.succ)).subtype (F(i.castSucc))) [def-weil-pbc-simple-module], exactly the required quotient. When r = 0 both adjacent-step conditions are vacuous, so the construction also includes the zero module.

lean.statement: theorem exists_simple_filtration_of_length_lt_top (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (hM : Module.length R M < ⊤) : ∃ (r : ℕ) (F : Fin (r + 1) → Submodule R M), F 0 = ⊥ ∧ F (Fin.last r) = ⊤ ∧ (∀ i : Fin r, F i.castSucc < F i.succ) ∧ (∀ i : Fin r, IsSimpleModule R (↥(F i.succ) ⧸ Submodule.comap (F i.succ).subtype (F i.castSucc)))
